parts.text: A committee of 3 members is chosen at random from a group of 8 people, which includes Alex and Ben. Find the probability that both Alex and Ben are chosen for the committee.
A bag contains 5 red balls and 4 blue balls. Three balls are selected at random without replacement. Find the probability that exactly 2 red balls and 1 blue ball are selected.

questions.title: Letter Arrangement with Fixed End Positions

parts.text: The 6 letters of the word ORANGE are arranged in a straight line at random. Find the probability that the arrangement begins with the letter O and ends with the letter E.

questions.title: Arrangement with Repeated Letters Grouped Together

parts.text: A random arrangement of the 6 letters of the word CHEESE is formed. Find the probability that all three Es are together.

questions.title: Equal Team Assignment for Two Named Individuals

parts.text: Ten students are divided at random into two teams of 5 players each, Team Red and Team Blue. Find the probability that two friends, Zara and Liam, are both placed in Team Red.

questions.title: Conditional Letter Adjacency Given Fixed Leading Letter

parts.text: A random arrangement of the 5 letters in the word APPLE is chosen. Given that the letter A is in the first position, find the probability that the two letter Ps are next to each other.

questions.title: Choir Quartet Selection by Voice Part

parts.text: A choir consists of 7 tenors and 5 basses. A quartet of 4 singers is chosen at random to perform an opening piece. Find the probability that the quartet consists of exactly 2 tenors and 2 basses.
Find the probability that the quartet contains no basses.

questions.title: Permutations of SUCCESS with Positional Restrictions

parts.text: A random arrangement of all 7 letters of the word SUCCESS is formed. Find the probability that the first letter is U and the last letter is E.
Find the probability that the three letter Ss are all together.

questions.title: Pen Selection Without Replacement and Colour Distribution

parts.text: A box contains 4 green pens, 5 black pens, and 3 blue pens. A student selects 3 pens at random without replacement. Find the probability that all 3 pens selected are of different colours.
Find the probability that at least 2 of the pens selected are green.

questions.title: Arrangements of ELEMENT with Separation and Conditional Restrictions

parts.text: A random arrangement of the 7 letters in the word ELEMENT is formed. Find the probability that the three letter Es are not all together.
Given that the arrangement begins with the letter L, find the probability that it ends with the letter T.

questions.title: Study Room Division and Twin Assignment

parts.text: A group of 12 students consists of 7 boys and 5 girls, including two twins, Sam and Tom. The 12 students are divided at random into two study groups of 6 students each, Room A and Room B. Find the probability that Sam and Tom are assigned to the same room.
Find the probability that Room A contains exactly 4 boys and 2 girls.

questions.title: Committee Selection with Seniority Constraints and Conditional Probability

parts.text: A committee of 5 people is to be selected at random from a club comprising 6 seniors, 5 juniors, and 4 novices. Find the probability that the committee contains no novices.
Find the probability that the committee contains at least 3 seniors.
Given that the committee contains no novices, find the probability that it contains at least 3 seniors.

questions.title: Arrangements of PARALLEL with Letter Clustering and Conditional Probabilities

parts.text: Consider random arrangements of the 8 letters in the word PARALLEL. Find the probability that the arrangement begins and ends with the letter L.
Find the probability that the three letter Ls are all together.
Given that the two letter As are together, find the probability that the three letter Ls are also all together.
